reasoning: This is the classic Pigeonhole Principle problem. We have 5 pigeons and only 4 holes, with the constraint that each hole can contain at most one pigeon. Since we need to assign each of the 5 pigeons to exactly one hole, and each hole can hold at most 1 pigeon, we can accommodate at most 4 pigeons total. It is mathematically impossible to place 5 pigeons into 4 holes with each hole containing at most one pigeon.
